title: Normalized comparison of principal Koszul Roos completion with dual Koszul presentations
statement: Let C be a small site and R a sheaf of commutative rings, with exact countable products of module sheaves. Choose derived categories for modules and strict inverse towers in the same morphism universe. Let a be any global section and P any cochain complex. Let D be any RingedKoszulLimitPresentation of the singleton list (a) [def-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-system]. Form the strict principal negative Koszul tensor tower V_n=[R --a^(n+1)--> R] tensor P [def-pur-principal-koszul-quotient-towers] and its shifted product cone H(V) [def-weil-strict-roos-model]. Its specified augmentation eta is the strict lift with zero shifted-product coordinate and degree-zero cone inclusions as product components. There exists an isomorphism e:Q(H(V)) ≅ D.completion(Q(P)) satisfying Q(eta) followed by e = D.unit(Q(P)). No regularity or K-flatness is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0A0E, proof of lemma-derived-completion-koszul: dual finite Koszul complexes and the inverse tensor tower; sites-cohomology.tex, Tag 0941, strict Roos augmentation normalization.

proof.text: For a singleton list the positive Koszul diagram is its two-term factor tensored with R[0]. Remove the tensor unit. In Hom of that factor into R[0], only one Hom-product component survives in each supported degree. Evaluate that component at one. The Hom differential dφ=d_Rφ-(-1)^q φd_K, in degrees -1 and 0, gives multiplication by a^(n+1). Thus this dual is the negative cone used for V_n. Dualizing the forward map (1,a) gives the inverse map (a,1). Dualizing the degree-zero projection gives the cone inclusion. Tensor symmetry changes P tensor dual to dual tensor P, with the standard total signs and no sign on the augmentation. These equations give an augmentation-compatible isomorphism of strict towers.

Apply the normalized strict Roos comparison to the two towers. Its naturality carries the strict tower isomorphism to the isomorphism of the displayed product cones and total derived inverse limits, and its augmentation clause carries the zero-coordinate lift to the specified derived-limit unit.

The unique normalized comparison between right-derived inverse-limit functors identifies the result with D.inverseLimit. Compose with D.tensorFactors at P. Naturality of the localized strict unit, applied to the specified representative isomorphism for Q(P), identifies this composite with D.unit(Q(P)). This produces the required isomorphism and unit equation. The finite free dual factors preserve quasi-isomorphisms. All equations remain valid for P=0, a=0 and a invertible.

theorem principalKoszulRoos_presentation_comparison
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ringedSiteModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R))]
    [HasExactLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) (ringedSiteModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R))]
    (a : (SheafOfModules.unit
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R)).sections)
    (P : CochainComplex (ringedSiteModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R)) ℤ)
    (D : RingedKoszulLimitPresentation R 1 (fun _ ↦ ⟨a.val, a.property⟩)) :
    ∃ e : DerivedCategory.Q.{w}.obj
        (roosF.obj (koszulTowerComplex R (koszulTensorTower R P a))) ≅
          D.completion.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.{w}.obj P),
      DerivedCategory.Q.{w}.map (principalKoszulRoosUnit R P a) ≫ e.hom =
        D.unit (DerivedCategory.Q.{w}.obj P)
